_comment: Relationship and implication edges for the seeded story, The Night Route.
Characters are named rather than keyed by id, because ids are generated at
startup. app/graph.py resolves them through Story.character_by_name.
`knows` edges are NOT here. They live in app/seed.py KNOWS, which stays the
one writer of what a character has been told, and graph.py lifts them into
An `implies` edge is fact to fact: a character who has been told the source
fact can reason to the target, so the horizon has to carry both. That is why
Maya can talk around the reassignment in scene 1 without anyone telling her.

relations.note: Nine years on the same shift. She signs his sheet every night.
By omission. She has the route sheet and she does not mention it.
To be told things straight, and early, the way he tells her.
That he not ask her directly, so she does not have to answer.

relations.dst_fact: That being in control of everything is not the same as being able to stop anything.
His wife, who packs him more food than he can eat.
The depot, which is cutting the route to make its numbers.
relations.note: She is the one who has to make the cut look like a schedule.

implies.src_fact: The night route is being cut at the end of the month.
implies.dst_fact: The depot is losing a night shift, so a driver is being moved off it.

implies.src_fact: The depot is losing a night shift, so a driver is being moved off it.
implies.dst_fact: Twenty-two years without an accident does not protect the driver who has them.

implies.src_fact: She was on shift and did not answer the phone the night her mother died.
implies.dst_fact: She believes being present is worth more than being right, and she has never said so out loud.
